PRIMARY CARE NOTE   Date: 2026-07-29
54F, general wellness examination.

S:
Patient presents for her yearly wellness visit. She reports feeling well overall and takes her blood pressure medication each morning, checking home readings twice a week. No shortness of breath. Diet includes frequent sugary drinks, which was discussed. She works as a librarian, mostly seated, and walks most evenings. Appetite is good, weight stable, and sleep is about 7 hours most nights. She has good support at home and asks about screening she is due for. Lives with her spouse. Never smoker, rare alcohol.

O:
BP 122/76, HR 70, RR 14, Temp 98.1 F, SpO2 99% on room air. Weight 162 lb, BMI 27.
General: well appearing, in no distress.
HEENT: normal.
Neck: no lymphadenopathy, no thyromegaly.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur, no gallop.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Abdomen: soft, nontender, no organomegaly.
Extremities: no edema, pulses intact.
Labs (prior week): basic metabolic panel normal, lipid panel within goal, A1c 6.0%.

A/P:
1. Essential hypertension, well controlled on current regimen. Continue lisinopril 10 mg daily. Home readings reviewed, averaging 122/76. Repeat basic metabolic panel in 12 months.
2. Prediabetes, counseled on diet and exercise. Reviewed reducing sugary drinks and adding regular walks. Recheck A1c in 6 months with a goal of modest weight loss.
3. Health maintenance: cervical screening up to date; mammography and colorectal screening discussed for her age. Influenza vaccine offered in the fall. Encouraged continued evening walks and light strength work.
4. Lifestyle: reviewed balanced meals, limiting sodium, consistent sleep, and adequate hydration.

Return in 12 months for the next wellness visit, sooner as needed.
